fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description: Detects the execution node.exe which is shipped with multiple software such as VMware, Adobe...etc. In order to execute arbitrary code. For example to establish reverse shell as seen in Log4j attacks...etc
fields.name: Potential Arbitrary Code Execution Via Node.EXE
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and ((tgt.process.image.path contains "\node.exe" and (tgt.process.cmdline contains " -e " or tgt.process.cmdline contains " --eval ")) and (tgt.process.cmdline contains ".exec(" and tgt.process.cmdline contains "net.socket" and tgt.process.cmdline contains ".connect" and tgt.process.cmdline contains "child_process")))
